appendix_title: Pack and Main p15 illustrated project source-cluster adjudication
review_type: Narrow independent source-only novelty appendix by the same reviewer after accepted94-question review; not a fresh-context full-bank rereview.

inspection.raw_packet_lines_reread: 1187–1247; complete initial packet reading retained in original report

inspection.scope: Only Pack and Main p15 project condition/reward clusters, plus the already accepted prompts/keys used for actual procedural comparison. No summaries, source audits, reader outputs/grades, or other reports read.

Q10.prompt_verbatim: Can money or other bonuses gained during an action pay for a later building, animal or association task in that action? How do immediate and after-finishing effects and simultaneous effects differ?
Q10.requested_scope_and_boundary: Requests immediate/after-finishing/simultaneous timing and sequential use of gains, not named Pack/project table values.

Q11.prompt_verbatim: Describe animal play requirements, payment with a matching partner zoo and double continent icons, standard and special enclosure occupancy, water/rock requirements and effect timing.
Q11.requested_scope_and_boundary: Requests animal play effects and matching Animal-card/partner-continent payment. It does not ask the named Reptile Breeding Program condition.

Q15.prompt_verbatim: Where do partner zoos and universities come from and go, can duplicates be acquired, how are bonuses handled, and what are partner and hand-limit restrictions?
Q15.requested_scope_and_boundary: Requests partner acquisition/placement/restrictions and bonuses, not the particular Reptile Breeding eligibility clause.

Q16.prompt_verbatim: How may a Conservation Project enter play, what are support conditions/once limits, where does its token come from, when is the uncovered bonus taken, and what happens to overflowing projects/tokens?
Q16.requested_scope_and_boundary: Requests support conditions, fulfilled unoccupied level, one-support limit, token source and rewards/bonuses. It supplies the project-support procedure but does not literally ask each illustrated condition or every numeric cell.

Q17.prompt_verbatim: For release projects, must printed standard enclosure size match exactly; what appeal/icons/reputation/conservation are lost or retained, and how do you free enclosure space?
Q17.requested_scope_and_boundary: Requests release eligibility by depicted printed-standard-size band and loss/retention/freeing priorities; its key explicitly retains ability-earned appeal, including the Pack example.

Q28.prompt_verbatim: Which animal categories count when an effect asks for animal categories, including bears and Petting Zoo animals?
Q28.requested_scope_and_boundary: Requests animal-category inclusion and bear/petting distinctions, not named project reward values.

Q30.prompt_verbatim: Which displayed symbols count as icons in your zoo, which do not, do effects count their own card and repeated icons, and which text wins if a card conflicts with a general rule?
Q30.requested_scope_and_boundary: Requests counted icons/locations, excluded condition symbols, self-counting and double-icon behavior. This directly asks the Pack paragraph self-counting rule and the icon sources used by ordinary count projects.

Q32.prompt_verbatim: Who gains the extra reputation on Release into the Wild projects, and how do Breeding Program projects differ in choosing a support space?
Q32.requested_scope_and_boundary: Requests release-project on-play reputation and the Breeding Program distinction: same condition for all three spaces, choose any free reward space. It does not literally request the printed reptile/partner relationship or every reward pair.

Q33.prompt_verbatim: How do you read an effect of the form X:Y when X has no number, says per, or lists numerical thresholds?
Q33.requested_scope_and_boundary: Requests per-fulfillment versus numbered/highest-threshold effect syntax. It supplies arithmetic interpretation, not a mandate to choose the highest condition on a project; project choice remains Q16/Q32.

Q34.prompt_verbatim: Define connected, isolated, border space, your zoo and any zoo.
Q34.requested_scope_and_boundary: Requests own-zoo versus any-zoo definition; Pack uses the own-zoo scope. Does not request Pack by name.

Q67.prompt_verbatim: How does Basic Research 207 count icons and reward its owner and the other players?
Q67.requested_scope_and_boundary: Requests different-icon counting for Basic Research; only supporting comparison of count operators, not a literal request for illustrated project values.

Q85.prompt_verbatim: How does WAZA Special Assignment 227 choose and find an animal, which animals become prohibited, and what rewards apply to small, large and size-3 animals?
Q85.requested_scope_and_boundary: Requests small/large/size-3 classification; key defines large as printed standard size4–5, supplying the Large Animals eligibility category.

Q127.prompt_verbatim: How do the partner-zoo condition, red max-25 appeal condition, minimum-reputation condition and minus-one-condition bonus work?
Q127.requested_scope_and_boundary: Requests how the partner-zoo condition works; its Animal branch is a partner from the same continent as the animal. That matching-continent predicate is the generic policy instantiated by the breeding illustration, although this prompt does not name that project.

exact_candidate_facts: Glossary p1 gives Pack as gain1appeal for each predator icon in your zoo.
The played predator counts its own predator icon, so Pack gives at least1additional appeal even with no other predator.
Main p9 illustrated Lion has Pack1: gain1appeal per predator in your zoo; the glossary makes the counted unit an icon.
Pack is an immediate ability award in addition to printed animal appeal; the Pack-earned appeal is not reversed when releasing the animal (Glossary p1 release clarification).

actual_procedural_coverage.coverage: Exact self-counting and repeated-icon policy, plus which own-zoo symbols count; the Pack paragraph is an express example of that policy.
Immediate animal ability resolution and printed track awards.
Per-fulfillment reward calculation and the own-zoo scope.
Retention of ability-earned appeal upon release.

clusters.literal_coverage_boundary: No accepted prompt asks the name Pack1 or the literal Lion multiplier. Those are retained here as printed lookup parameters; generic procedure coverage does not mean every named ability text is literally requested.
clusters.reason: Changing the counted category to predator, the multiplier to1 and the named source to Lion supplies no new choice, target-selection policy, timing, priority, cap or exception beyond the actually requested policies. The self-inclusion example is directly requested in Q30; the release-retention branch is directly requested in Q17.

clusters.cluster: B Main p15 illustrated projects including Reptile Breeding Program

printed_lookup_evidence.condition: Count reptile icons in your zoo.
Count large animals in your zoo; large is printed standard-enclosure requirement4–5 under the existing size definition.
Count water icons in your zoo, including counted top-left requirements under Q30.

visible_tiers_left_to_right.source_boundary: The middle condition is obscured by the yellow player token in the p15 illustration. No numeric requirement inferred from unsupplied card text.

printed_lookup_evidence.condition: Release1animal with an Africa icon; match depicted printed-standard-size band.

printed_lookup_evidence.condition_verbatim: Requires1reptile and a partner zoo of the same continent.
printed_lookup_evidence.eligibility_reading: Have a reptile in your zoo and a partner zoo matching that reptile’s continent; the same eligibility condition applies to all three support spaces.
printed_lookup_evidence.reward_source_corroboration: Glossary p1 explicitly contrasts2conservation with2reputation and only1conservation for a later supporter.
printed_lookup_evidence.request_message_correction: The follow-up task message described the middle reward as2conservation+1reputation; direct p15 visual and Glossary p1 instead show1conservation+2reputation. This is printed-data precision, not a new branch or a bank-key defect.

actual_procedural_coverage.coverage: Fulfill a currently unoccupied depicted condition, choose a satisfied support level, place map-left token, receive depicted reward; normal once-per-project restriction.
Count the specified icon in the own zoo using the requested counted/excluded symbol rules; water requirements count, left play conditions do not.
Release by depicted bands, loss/retention/freeing rules, and extra reputation only when bringing the release project into play.
Breeding Program same eligibility condition at all three spaces and any-free-space choice; reward differences do not change eligibility.
Matching the relevant animal’s continent to an owned partner zoo; ordinary Animal-card partner matching is already an actual requested policy.

breeding_relational_condition_challenge.possible_gap_considered: Does requiring a reptile and a partner zoo of that reptile’s continent add an unasked cross-object eligibility branch beyond mere icon counts?
breeding_relational_condition_challenge.earlier_prompt_limit: Q16 does not literally request this particular condition. Q127 applies the matching-partner policy to an Animal condition; it does not name the breeding project. A literal request for the exact reptile/partner predicate therefore cannot be claimed.
breeding_relational_condition_challenge.independent_reason: The printed predicate selects an existing eligible animal type and instantiates the already requested same-continent animal/partner relation, then applies the already requested project support gate. It does not change what continent matching means, require a new ordering of acquisition, alter partner availability, demand a second worker, release/consume the reptile, introduce a new zone or timing window, or modify the equal-condition/free-reward-space breeding policy. Thus its unasked named eligibility data is a mechanical instantiation rather than a distinct procedure or exception.

clusters.literal_coverage_boundary: The earlier prompts request procedures and some definitions, not every named project condition, all exact thresholds, or each reward cell. This appendix preserves the visible printed data as lookup evidence without asserting literal all-cell coverage. No requirement to choose the highest available project tier is imported from Q33; Q16/Q32 govern project choice.
clusters.reason: Reptiles and Aquatic replace only the counted icon and printed amounts. Large Animals substitutes a defined eligibility category. Serengeti supplies Africa and reward values while using already requested release bands and priorities. Reptile Breeding Program combines the established matching relation with the explicitly requested equal-condition/any-free-space support rule. None adds a distinct outcome branch, consequential timing, priority or exception under the supplied strict-novelty criterion.

final_verdict: Neither examined cluster establishes a distinct unasked procedural rule, source-defined outcome branch, or consequential timing/priority/exception. Preserve visible printed facts and the breeding predicate as lookup evidence; zero new question credit. Prior full acceptance is preserved, with the independent appendix scope limited to these two clusters.
independence: No other reports, summary/source-audit materials, reader outputs or grades opened. No readers contacted. Parent-supplied values were checked against raw sources rather than accepted as evidence. Own previous acceptance history preserved.
